messages.subject: Pattern identification
parts:
Good afternoon....


I'm running a sizable number of clustering operations. In particular, the KMeans and PAM cluster algorithms are somewhat path dependent depending on the seed values used for selecting their starting centroid/medioids. As a result I can get multiple different responses if I don't fix my seed values. And, as it happens, I'm finding that there can be substantial differences in the resulting clusters that result in some of those solutions being more useful to me than others.

Is there a good way given a list of (for example) 100 vectors each with cluster membership of each sample point to identify the set of unique solutions and how many times that solution was arrived at? 

This is complicated by there being no guarantee that even given the "same solution" that the clusters will be identified the same way. i.e. in vector A and vector B which both grouped the same samples together into a cluster with the same members, in A that cluster might be cluster #1 and in B cluster #2.

I'm more of a python programmer by practice, and I'd do it in python by looping through all of the vectors, and replace the first cluster in the vector with another name (like "A") and propagate that change through the entirety of that vector for every member of that cluster, and then do the same with the second and so on with "B", "C"... Then I'd be able to compare them directly in a doable if ugly looping structure.

I have a suspicion that R should be able to handle this in a more elegant fashion. Suggestions are very welcome.

Nate

Nate,

This was an interesting one. I think this gets at what you are trying to do.

library(plyr)
set.seed(0)
# Generate the data - this creates a list of a bunch of character vectors
data = alply(1:100, 1, function(x) sample(c("A", "B"), 3, replace=TRUE))

# Use laply to across all the vectors to switch labels

# Converts 
strings = laply(data, function(x) {
  uniques = unique(x)                  # This block renames the
  ints = 1:length(uniques)             # characters so they are in ascending
                                       # alphabetical order
  names(ints) = uniques
  fixed = sort(uniques)[ints[x]]
  return(paste(fixed, collapse= " "))  # This collapses each vector into a string
})


# Tally up the unique strings
counts = table(strings)
counts

## strings
## A A A A A B A B A A B B B B B 
##    14    29    21    24    12

#I'm not sure how what to do with the output, but this gets you a list of
#the unique vectors
unique_vectors = strsplit(names(counts), " ")
unique_vectors

## [[1]]
## [1] "A" "A" "A"
## 
## [[2]]
## [1] "A" "A" "B"
## 
## [[3]]
## [1] "A" "B" "A"
## 
## [[4]]
## [1] "A" "B" "B"
## 
## [[5]]
## [1] "B" "B" "B"

Hey, folks,

Thanks for the help, but Vince is correct. Your solution is close, but doesn't handle the label switch case very well. Is there an upcoming R user group session that I could use to demo the challenge since I think that'll be more effective than trying to describe it textually?


Here's the code I'm playing with at the moment. Basically what it does is read in a set of demographic data from csv, iterate through seed values 1:100 conducing Kmeans clustering, and saving the outputs to a list. It then implements Noam's suggestion, and appends the resulting unique vectors to the shapefile. In this case it comes up with 53 unique vectors, though quite a few are permutations of the label switch issue. Finally it joins the items together and writes it out to a shapefile.

I'm not particularly elegant with my R yet, so I also welcome stylistic suggestions. 

Thank you,
Nate

# Load libraries
library(psych)
library(nFactors)
library(plyr)

#Kmeans function
kmeanscluster <- function(seed,indf,numclus,maxiters){
  set.seed(seed)
  fit <- kmeans(indf, numclus,iter.max=maxiters) 
  aggregate(indf,by=list(fit$cluster),FUN=mean) 
  return(fit$cluster)
}


# Read in the table
tracts <-read.table("walk_bike.csv",header=TRUE, sep=",",colClasses=c("character",rep("numeric",11)))
# Select just the fields to use for the clustering
natracts <-na.omit(tracts)
wtracts <-natracts[c(2:11)]
geoids <- natracts[c(1)]
colnames(geoids) <- c("GEOID10")

# Run Kmeans, no factor analysis
seeds <- 1:100
t <- lapply(seeds,kmeanscluster,indf=wtracts,4, maxiters=20)
# Prep for join to Shapefile
seeds_df <- data.frame(do.call("cbind",t))
colnames(seeds_df) <-c(paste("sd_",seeds,sep=""))
seeds_df <- data.frame(geoids,seeds_df)

# Noam's code
sets = laply(t, function(x) {

uniques = unique(x)                  # This block renames the
  ints = 1:length(uniques)             # characters so they are in ascending
                                       # alphabetical order
  names(ints) = uniques
fixed = ints[x]

return(paste(fixed, collapse= " "))  # This collapses each vector into a string
})

# Tally up the unique strings

counts = table(sets)
# counts # A bit much to actually inspect visually

#I'm not sure how what to do with the output, but this gets you a list of
#the unique vectors
unique_vectors = strsplit(names(counts), " ")
unique_vectors

num_uv <- length(unique_vectors)
# End Noam's code


# Compile unique vectors for attaching to the shapefile.
uv_df <- data.frame(do.call("cbind",unique_vectors))
colnames(uv_df) <-c(paste("uf_",1:num_uv,sep=""))
uv_df <- data.frame(geoids,uv_df)



# Load Shape
library(rgdal)
tracts_o <- readOGR(dsn=".", layer="tl_2010_06_tract10")
tracts_o <- merge(x=tracts_o, y=seeds_df, by = "GEOID10", all.x = TRUE)
tracts_o <- merge(x=tracts_o, y=uv_df, by = "GEOID10", all.x = TRUE)
writeOGR(tracts_o, ".", "seedtest4",driver="ESRI Shapefile")

Hey, folks,

Thanks for the help, but Vince is correct. Your solution is close, but doesn't handle the label switch case very well. Is there an upcoming R user group session that I could use to demo the challenge since I think that'll be more effective than trying to describe it textually?


Here's the code I'm playing with at the moment. Basically what it does is read in a set of demographic data from csv, iterate through seed values 1:100 conducing Kmeans clustering, and saving the outputs to a list. It then implements Noam's suggestion, and appends the resulting unique vectors to the shapefile. In this case it comes up with 53 unique vectors, though quite a few are permutations of the label switch issue. Finally it joins the items together and writes it out to a shapefile.

I'm not particularly elegant with my R yet, so I also welcome stylistic suggestions. 

Thank you,
Nate

# Load libraries
library(psych)
library(nFactors)
library(plyr)

#Kmeans function
kmeanscluster <- function(seed,indf,numclus,maxiters){
  set.seed(seed)
  fit <- kmeans(indf, numclus,iter.max=maxiters) 
  aggregate(indf,by=list(fit$cluster),FUN=mean) 
  return(fit$cluster)
}


# Read in the table
tracts <-read.table("walk_bike.csv",header=TRUE, sep=",",colClasses=c("character",rep("numeric",11)))
# Select just the fields to use for the clustering
natracts <-na.omit(tracts)
wtracts <-natracts[c(2:11)]
geoids <- natracts[c(1)]
colnames(geoids) <- c("GEOID10")

# Run Kmeans, no factor analysis
seeds <- 1:100
t <- lapply(seeds,kmeanscluster,indf=wtracts,4, maxiters=20)
# Prep for join to Shapefile
seeds_df <- data.frame(do.call("cbind",t))
colnames(seeds_df) <-c(paste("sd_",seeds,sep=""))
seeds_df <- data.frame(geoids,seeds_df)

# Noam's code
sets = laply(t, function(x) {
  uniques = unique(x)                  # This block renames the
  ints = 1:length(uniques)             # characters so they are in ascending
                                       # alphabetical order
  names(ints) = uniques
  fixed = ints[x]
  return(paste(fixed, collapse= " "))  # This collapses each vector into a string
})

# Tally up the unique strings
counts = table(sets)
# counts # A bit much to actually inspect visually

#I'm not sure how what to do with the output, but this gets you a list of
#the unique vectors
unique_vectors = strsplit(names(counts), " ")
unique_vectors
num_uv <- length(unique_vectors)
# End Noam's code


# Compile unique vectors for attaching to the shapefile.
uv_df <- data.frame(do.call("cbind",unique_vectors))
colnames(uv_df) <-c(paste("uf_",1:num_uv,sep=""))
uv_df <- data.frame(geoids,uv_df)



# Load Shape
library(rgdal)
tracts_o <- readOGR(dsn=".", layer="tl_2010_06_tract10")
tracts_o <- merge(x=tracts_o, y=seeds_df, by = "GEOID10", all.x = TRUE)

Nate
